cinder_husk.subject: Cinder Husk — What remains when a fire is given a body and the body is given nothing else.

tallow_wisp.subject: Tallow Wisp — A votive flame that outlived its prayer and now searches for someone to grieve.

thread_leech.subject: Thread-Leech — It does not want your blood; it wants the thing that binds you, and it is patient.

reliquary_mite.subject: Reliquary Mite — Small enough to live inside a saint's knucklebone, and old enough to have eaten the saint.

sexton.subject: Sexton of the Undercroft — He still digs the graves, though no one has died here in a hundred years who stayed dead.

mourner.subject: The Mourner — It weeps for every soul that fought alone, and it will make mourners of you both if you give it the chance.

votive_throng.subject: Votive Throng — A hundred small flames lit for the dead, still burning long after anyone remained to want them answered.

gravewax_husk.subject: Gravewax Husk — The tallow of old funerals, melted down and poured into the rough shape of someone it half remembers.

pallbearer.subject: Pallbearer — It still carries the coffin, and it has decided, after all these years, that the coffin should not be empty.

warden_of_the_crossing.subject: Warden of the Crossing — It stands where two paths meet and will not say which of you it has come to collect, because it has not decided.

interred_saint.subject: The Interred Saint — They buried her with honors, then with chains, then with the whole of the Undercroft, and none of it was enough.

psalm_eater.subject: Psalm-Eater — It swallowed every prayer this place ever raised, and it is still hungry for whatever passes between you.

bell_husk.subject: Bell Husk — A bell that was rung once too often, now wearing the bellringer, still tolling a note that unravels things.

lectern_wretch.subject: Lectern Wretch — Bent over a book whose pages were eaten centuries ago, it reads your fervor back to you, word for word.

chorister_low.subject: Chorister of the Low Note — It holds the note beneath hearing, the one you feel in the floor of your chest like a second pulse.

chorister_mid.subject: Chorister of the Held Note — It has sustained the same note since the choir died, and it will not breathe until the song is finished.

chorister_high.subject: Chorister of the High Note — The descant that was meant to carry the dead upward, still climbing, with nothing left to carry.

the_cantor.subject: The Cantor — It conducts whether or not anyone sings, and it can hear, precisely, every place your voices fail to meet.

bellkeeper.subject: The Bellkeeper — Each toll names one of you, and it has kept the bell oiled all these years for exactly this occasion.

choirmaster.subject: The Choirmaster — The Choir went hollow the day it demanded one voice from many, and it has been rehearsing you since you arrived.

the_unraveled.subject: The Unraveled — It was bound to someone once, and it remembers the cut better than the binding, and it wants you to remember it too.

character_vess.subject: Vess, the Hexweaver — quiet, precise spirit-binder who stitches curses into things; violet accent

character_bram.subject: Bram, the Cinderfist — loud, kinetic spirit-binder who fights like an argument he is winning; ember accent

character_witness.subject: The Witness — a long-dead spirit bound to a thread, a disdainful long-suffering steward; pale lavender accent

title_splash.subject: Two spirit-binders at the mouth of the descent, seen from behind, a single luminous soul-thread strung between their wrists, the jammed funeral-machine's stair falling away into the dark below them — the game's thesis in one image; gold-thread accent
